name: Lumae Analysis
author: Lumae
description: Mirrors supported Navidrome and Jellyfin catalogues and prepares Lumae volume, SmoothFade, album-similarity, and artist-similarity data away from the phone.

versions.changelog: Analysis workers: a file cancelled while its analysis worker was still starting is no longer analyzed anyway (it could run to its time limit after Lumae had moved on), and a file cancelled while a worker failed to start no longer runs inside AudioMuse's process without the time limit. Each runner turn that analyzes files now logs how many it analyzes at once and why (the setting, cores, memory, a container's limit, memory available) and, when it ends, the analysis processes it used, their largest peak memory and any left running, so a question about Lumae's processes or memory can be answered from AudioMuse's log. Nothing on the wire changes. Includes every 1.9.0 change. AudioMuse 3.2.0 is still the minimum.

Lumae leaves AudioMuse's task queue: two runners of its own, one in AudioMuse's web process and one in a worker (the Heavy work setting says which does the heavy analysis), do the background work. An analysis you start runs at once, a worker that is switched off no longer blocks AudioMuse, and Lumae steps aside while AudioMuse analyses, cleans or migrates. Catalogue work runs in a short-lived child process, so the web process keeps its memory and speed. Lumae's schedules, and any task an older version left queued, are removed on install. New songs reach the phone without waiting for a busy AudioMuse: a refresh request is kept and served (contract §2.5), and a changed catalogue projects its analysis at once. Similar albums and artists are published on a library that keeps changing (§2.6) and rebuilt at most every 6 hours. Less repeated work: files that cannot be analyzed stop being retried, credits re-checks are spread out, and the identity recheck runs only while needed. Journeys: Lumae's listening journeys are kept on the server, so they survive a reinstall and follow you to another phone (capabilities.journeys, §5.7), gated by Living Collections. The settings page's counts of loudness and edges left are current. Includes every 1.8.0 change. AudioMuse 3.2.0 is still the minimum.

Whole-track loudness for Lumae's volume normalization (ITU-R BS.1770-4, measured in the edge pass's decode or by a low-priority backfill; a new loudness stream; albums pooled once every track is measured). Faster background analysis: the edge and loudness passes work until the watchdog tick's deadline; up to 4 files are analysed at once inside the one tick (setting "Files analyzed at once", auto), each in its own worker at nice 10; one download and one analysis call per track give the waveform, edge and loudness together, downloaded by Lumae as the original file (Navidrome format=raw, Jellyfin static=true) outside AudioMuse's TEMP_DIR; credits re-checks back off and idle ticks do less; the settings page shows throughput, ETA and refused schedules. After installing, the loudness backfill measures the whole library once. A file still being analysed at a tick's deadline now finishes instead of restarting every tick, so long tracks no longer stall a parallel pass. AudioMuse's Scheduled Tasks lists only Lumae's five schedules, each with an info tooltip on hosts that show one; the settings page explains them. AudioMuse 3.2.0 is still the minimum.

The analysis-run finalization's catalogue refresh does far less database work: it reads the changed tracks of the generation it is writing in one pass (the per-track lookup filtered the whole generation for each one) and writes the generation a page of rows per statement instead of one row per statement. A 36k-track refresh with about 5,500 changed tracks went from 86-103 s to 34 s in local tests, so the watchdog tick that finalizes an AudioMuse analysis run holds AudioMuse's schedules back far less. Lumae's other schedules (catalogue refresh, analysis projection, provider identity recheck, collection retention) now say what they did in AudioMuse's task message instead of "Plugin task completed successfully."; the settings page no longer says AudioMuse labels these tasks "Songs analyzed: 0". AudioMuse 3.2.0 is still the minimum.

SmoothFade: edge profiles in schema v3 on request (edge_schema=3; health edge_profiles.schema_versions lists 3 once every stored edge has its v3 digest), without the windows' sample peak and spectral flux and with their own digest. When a song's music ends before its last 30 seconds (a hidden track after a long silence, a long silent run-out), the v3 edge says where and carries an ending window measured before it, so Lumae fades on the real ending. v2 transfers and stored edges are unchanged. Scheduler: the catalogue watchdog steps aside while AudioMuse has a refused schedule to retry or one of its main jobs running and comes back 5-15 minutes later, so AudioMuse's nightly analysis and clustering and Lumae's other schedules no longer fail after 240 minutes blocked; minute cadence skips Lumae's other schedules; a tick works for at most 45 s over several actions; the edge pass finds its tracks by key (639 to 125 ms on a 36k-track library); disabling Lumae's schedules on the Scheduled Tasks page lasts; each tick says what it did. Neither the per-song hook during an AudioMuse analysis run nor the waveform backfill queues an edge task per song any more; the library pass makes those edges, and on-demand requests still get theirs at once. AudioMuse 3.2.0 is still the minimum.

Storage: MusicBrainz responses for credits are cached for 3 days instead of 30 and deleted as soon as they expire, and the upgrade deletes those cached longer by earlier versions (on a 36k-track library about 1.1 GB of a 3.7 GB AudioMuse backup). Profile journal events written before 1.3.0's edge references drop their copy of the edge when that edge is still stored; every reader serves them exactly as before. Credits versions are compacted to two snapshots of the catalogue's albums instead of 50,000 versions. Nothing on the wire changes; that library's backup went from 3.7 to 2.5 GB.

Jellyfin: Lumae Analysis mirrors a Jellyfin 12.0 or later library next to Navidrome (supported_provider_types jellyfin and navidrome), reading each music library inside the bound AudioMuse server with that server's own credentials, and binds each Jellyfin catalogue to its server Id from /System/Info/Public: another server, product, release or server type blocks the catalogue and is never adopted; as for Navidrome from 1.5.1, a probe that fails stores only its error and the refresh never reads an unverified server. Health adds provider_server_id and provider_version per source. A moved, renamed or re-cased Jellyfin file keeps its identity: a missing track is held for 14 days and, when AudioMuse maps a new ID to the same content fingerprint, the move is published as an atomic provider_identity_rekey_v2 (journal rekeys and a manifest; collections, shelves, Vibes, covers and profiles follow). Tags Jellyfin does not expose (release type, compilation, explicit, credits with roles, ISRC, disc subtitle, original date, ReplayGain gains and peaks, BPM, sort names) are read from the original files and published under the OpenSubsonic keys Navidrome uses. Health keeps every applied rekey (last_applied_transition_id and retained_transitions) and each v2 manifest names its previous_transition_id. Emby and Lyrion are removed. Navidrome behaviour is unchanged. Includes every 1.5.1 fix.

A slow or failed Navidrome ping no longer pauses sync: up to 1.5.0 one failed provider ping closed catalogue and analysis sync for the Lumae app and failed the analysis projection until a catalogue refresh, up to 30 minutes later. Now only the error is stored (shown under Provider identity safety); the call that saw it still fails closed, and the next verified ping lifts the hold. The analysis_projection task reports a by-design hold (identity unverified or pending, AudioMuse migration not ready, no published catalogue) as deferred instead of failing. MusicBrainz lookups run on the catalogue watchdog instead of an every-minute cron task that flooded AudioMuse's Recent tasks list. The settings page drops the AudioMuse upgrade-sequence diagnostic, which AudioMuse can no longer feed.

Custom covers: the Lumae app and Lumae Radio keep the cover a person chose for a saved Vibe, a Living Collection or a playlist in step through GET /api/covers/changes and POST /api/covers/mutations: an album from inside it, an orb colour or a photo. Covers are revisioned records scoped by account and catalogue like saved Vibes, and a delete means back to the automatic cover. Photos go to a small image store (POST /api/covers/images, GET /api/covers/image): JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 512 KB, named by their SHA-256; an image no cover uses is deleted after two days. Health advertises capabilities.covers.

Saved Vibe sync: the Lumae app keeps its saved Palette, Mood Compass and DNA Vibes in step across devices through GET /api/vibes/changes and POST /api/vibes/mutations, scoped by account and catalogue like Album Shelf and switched on by the Living Collections setting. Writes are revision-checked (409 vibe_conflict with the current record), deletes are tombstones, and receipts replay a lost response for 30 days. Health advertises capabilities.vibes.

Profile bootstrap create adoption: a retried create (same client_request_id) takes over the snapshot its own earlier create already captured, instead of capturing the whole library again. Fixes large libraries (about 132k profiles) whose first profile load never finished because the in-request capture outlasted the app's request timeout. Health advertises profile_bootstrap.create_adoption.

Artist portraits in the catalogue: a Navidrome scan reads getArtists once per selected music folder and publishes each album artist's coverArt as artists.cover_art_id, so the Lumae app no longer looks up every artist from the phone. A changed portrait republishes the artist; guests and a failed lookup keep the published portrait.

Saved (deferred) on-demand requests are served within about a minute on an otherwise idle server: a deferral wakes the reconcile watchdog, and its schedule counts deferred work as ready until it is served (they waited for the next hourly tick).

Edge library pass starts within a minute of a qualified worker report or a catalogue refresh with changes (it waited for the next idle hourly tick); a worker's periodic runtime report no longer cancels a finished pass's six-hour re-sweep delay.

Journal fences and integrity health (upgrade: docs/runbooks/UPGRADE_1.3.md); gzip transport (K1); v2 bootstrap edge references, sliding expiry, truthful availability, idempotent create (K2-K5); edge_refs in the profile stream (K6); collections feed epoch and conflicts (K8-K10); edge profiles on stock AudioMuse via PyAV self-qualification, worker-reported analyzable, server edge library pass, on-demand priority with deferred requests, edge_status; vectors served for pruned analysis generations.
Set fully_verified to False when transition blocks catalog sync to preserve progressive readiness contract.
Verify release type and complete single/EP recording membership for duplicate-safe Lumae recommendations.

Complete personal discovery feedback: sync album-specific memories with artist context and explicit enjoyment independently of nostalgia recognition. Advertise both capabilities for safe upgrades from 1.2.2.

Add catalogue-independent personal discovery sync with field conflicts, tombstones and epoch recovery. Add external MusicBrainz entity jobs with playback priority, cancellation and a persistent 80-request daily allowance per account. Existing shelf and credits APIs remain compatible.

Remove retired Radio DJ analysis, routes, worker registrations, and dependencies. Clean up legacy DJ tables and schedules on upgrade while preserving catalog, loudness, SmoothFade edge profiles, collections, credits, and relationship data. Stop old dedicated DJ workers before upgrading.

Add Personal Shelves synchronization and insights, MusicBrainz credits enrichment, resumable relationship builds, source-bound edge profiles, and opt-in DJ analysis with bounded queue deferral and interrupted-work recovery. Preserve the Navidrome identity guard from 1.1.9. DJ analysis requires a compatible dedicated worker and remains disabled by default.

Allow trusted pre-canonical Navidrome releases to publish ordinary catalogue removals and library-scope changes instead of misclassifying them as incomplete provider-ID migrations; preserve fail-closed inspection for pending or blocked identity transitions.

Reduce reconcile dashboard noise with adaptive active, waiting, retry, and hourly-idle schedules; add bounded Lumae-owned action progress and history; and back off failed work independently without losing restart recovery.

Restore AudioMuse 3.4 compatibility by removing private RQ imports and replacing task-within-task queueing with a database-driven one-action reconciliation watchdog; recover stranded analysis runs and make profile, relationship, catalogue, and provider follow-ups restart-safe.

Recover automatically when AudioMuse rolls back a failed plugin install-hook transaction: retry the additive provider-identity schema on Flask startup and restore PostgreSQL transaction health when the optional status panel cannot be read.

Make projection release durable across mixed old/new worker startup: plugin migration records a database reconciliation request, argument-compatible startup and scheduled rechecks retry it, and only a successful atomic projection clears it.

Close the plugin-upgrade ordering race by forcing one idempotent analysis-projection check after install, even when Flask startup already marked the completed AudioMuse migration ready; recurring rechecks remain no-op once reconciled.

Allow a completed AudioMuse provider migration to hand off legitimate post-analysis fingerprint relinks to the normal atomic analysis projection while retaining the protected pre-transition generation; contradictory duplicate mappings still fail closed.

Treat Navidrome prerelease, snapshot, branch, and unknown builds as uncertain transition builds so canonical-ID inspection runs even when a develop build retains the last safe numeric version, and canonicalize unordered contributor records so the required two stable scans cannot be reset by equivalent provider row ordering.
Fix PostgreSQL catalogue refresh locking so provider-identity inspection locks only mandatory rows and safely preserves the last complete catalogue while optional analysis state is joined.

Detect, shield, and publish exact Navidrome canonical-ID transitions after two stable scans; preserve Lumae analysis and user state atomically; retain recovery evidence; gate fresh AudioMuse projection ingestion until its provider migration is healthy; and prune superseded snapshots plus bounded cursor journals without invalidating active bootstrap leases.

Bound waveform decoding and filtering memory, cap every background job, make installs idempotent, limit backfill and catalogue batches, replace all-pairs relationships with bounded IVF shortlists, preserve failed-projection and registry-source retry recovery, and add a maintenance pause that preserves published data.
Replace release-number approval with live API and data-contract admission, while preserving independent catalogue browsing and progressive sonic enrichment.
Normalize structured provider artist identities before publishing catalogue and relationship data, and rebuild existing catalogues so similar-artist keys remain readable and addressable.
Version catalogue fingerprints with atomic epoch rebases, expose preparation start/status routes, and publish transfer-cost diagnostics for safe mobile planning.

Replace manual fresh/upgrade attestations with automatic evidence-based verification, and present four clear statuses for Library, AudioMuse source analysis, Volume & ramps, and Lumae similar-album/artist relationships.
Durably reconcile missed and failed catalogue repairs, attest the worker and catalogue-builder versions before declaring publication current, and keep repeated setup checks idempotent.

Move album and artist relationship preparation to AudioMuse using Lumae's native scoring model, publish relationship and playback-profile cursor streams, and keep all enrichment asynchronous so catalogue setup finishes immediately.

Map every Navidrome track to provider music folders even when no folder filter is configured, replace large N+1 album hydration scans with bounded folder and song pagination, reject partial or unknown memberships, and automatically rebuild affected catalogue generations.

Preserve selected Navidrome folder memberships through catalogue hydration, automatically prepare and repair catalogues through an idempotent mobile API, keep published generations available during refresh, and rebuild safely after catalogue-builder upgrades.

Prevent selected Navidrome music folders from producing an empty catalogue, reject every zero-track publication, and make required app-sync readiness unmistakable before separate sonic verification and optional waveform work.

Keep repair-flagged AudioMuse 3 mappings usable as provisional sonic links, preserve their conflict evidence for automatic replacement, reproject automatically after update, avoid unchanged journal churn, and make Firefox-safe GET status polling.
Sync AudioMuse 3 sonic links progressively while Chromaprint backfills, keep incomplete groups usable unless they definitely disagree, and add a read-only source-scoped database state dashboard.
Complete v2-to-v3 source rebinding before readiness checks, accept only proven legacy aliases, and prevent stale legacy tasks from reaching the AudioMuse 3 registry.
Qualify AudioMuse 3.0.4 and 3.0.5 with exact patch-bound readiness acknowledgements while keeping later 3.x releases fail-closed.
Make Lumae usable as soon as the Navidrome catalogue and AudioMuse projection publish; move waveform coverage to bounded background batches and prioritize current playback tracks.
Provide a Navidrome-only, source-safe catalogue with Prepare Lumae and one coalesced catalogue, projection, and profile update per AudioMuse analysis run.
Qualify AudioMuse 3.0.3 with source-scoped Chromaprint coverage, repair-sequence diagnostics, and an administrator-controlled sync readiness gate.
Add the provider-authoritative catalogue capability and a dual AudioMuse 2.6/v3 compatibility handshake.
Make personal versus shared collection scope explicit and add principal-scoped, checksummed JSON backups with full-library and per-collection export plus safe additive restore in the web manager.
Fix the collection library track query on PostgreSQL by sorting on the source author column instead of a nested SELECT alias, restoring initial browsing and search.

Replace the basic add dialog with an art-first Albums, Tracks, and Artists library workbench; add categorized search, artist and album drill-down, provider track/disc numbers, bulk collection management, cover art, and credential-safe audio previews.
Expose enabled Living Collections in the Plugins menu, restore opaque high-contrast dialogs, and fix Add music requests so selected albums and tracks are persisted with visible progress and errors.
Add opt-in Living Collections with mixed album and track membership, a responsive AudioMuse manager, per-user storage, revisions, idempotent mutations, and incremental sync.
Vectorize the BS.1770 biquad filter with SciPy so loudness and MixRamp profiles are ready before playback catches the analysis queue.
Add Queue Whole Library to enqueue every missing, stale, or changed Lumae profile in 250-track worker jobs while keeping Catch Up Now for one batch.
